text: The stage of life from 15 to 21, a time of service when an apprentice knows enough to assist his master in the lab.
A periodic roll determining a character's aging, modified by Healthy or Unhealthy environmental features at a covenant.
Fourth caliph and son-in-law of Muhammad; first imam for the Shi'is, recipient of Dhu'l-Fiqar.
Angel who carries men away at death; Shinnui Shem hides a man from him by changing his name.
Personal power allowing a humanoid faerie of size -2 to +2 to look and feel human via illusion; used by the Man in Black with a Sack on His Back.
Nunnery near Paris to which Héloïse moved.
Jews in Christian lands, mostly France and Germany, socially isolated and turned towards theology and mysticism.
Table rolled when the yearly aura modifier is -4 or less, with outcomes from vanished regio levels to permanent aura decrease.
Figure to whom Michael appeared (Numbers 22).
Massed-combat story event used to resolve escalades and sieges, rated with Man, Size and Enemy components and an Event Bonus.
Vassal of Fudarus (822-969) on Mount Beauvray that revived a cult of Vercingetorix and was destroyed by Wizard Wars from Montverte magi.
A Major Supernatural Virtue granting angelic descent, increased Size, very slow aging, and Dominion Lore, but heavy food requirements and many restrictions.
A Major Supernatural Flaw: the character cannot survive in the mundane world and must live in a supernatural aura of 5 or greater of a chosen realm to stay healthy.
A Templar Status Virtue for a it of the Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon, replaceable by Templar Administrator.
Major magus of the Loch Leglean Tribunal from the covenant of Crun Clach.
A Minor General Flaw: the character is reckless with a particular Ability, treating any rolled zero as a botch when using it.
A Virtue that enhances medical skill, reducing the risk of botches when using the Medicine Ability.
French king who made an accord with Rollo in 911.
A first-century Jewish tentmaker converted by Saint Paul in Corinth whose Roman house became a church; he and his wife were martyred.
A Minor Hermetic Flaw: the magus has trouble targeting spells, with aiming rolls of 0 automatically botching and -3 to Finesse rolls.
UnGifted gruagach and hunter, blamed for every mishap, who shapeshifts into a bear and studies under Domhnall.
A Supernatural Ability allowing the character to temporarily revive and command a relatively intact, unburied corpse.
Terrain protecting against attacks, giving +3 to +12 Defense.
The it or it, a slender sight-hunting dog kept by most Highland households to hunt and protect herds.
Founder of the monastery of St. Denis in the 7th century.
A score that increases like an Ability as a character accumulates Aging Points; at 4 the character is frail and must roll on the Crisis Table, and at 5 is bedridden.
A type of Mythic Companion created by powerful demons as weapons in the conflict between Heaven and Hell; tragic figures with Hellish powers but free will.
Exception granted by bishop or pope, e.g. for priests not meeting ordination criteria.
City with a great keep of the Counts of Flanders.
The imbalanced state of humors producing a patient's symptoms, which a physician must understand to bring the humors back into balance.

Overlord of Aquitaine who attended the Second Crusade with a guard of female knights dressed as Amazons; her scandalous behavior led to a Papal Bull barring women from the Third Crusade. An example of inheritance-based female power.
Magic items churches may possess, costing 1 Build Point per level.
Secret variations on standard Hermetic magic practiced by those who belong to Mystery Cults.
Experience points gained from casual attendance at preaching, even in unknown Abilities.
Spontaneous faerie spells requiring a Faerie Method, Faerie Power, and applicable Sympathy Trait; effects are never permanent.
The few Abilities, usually Methods and Powers, that a holy tradition favors; characters with True Faith may study them without the Supernatural Ability penalty.
A leadership title of the Seirenes won at a grand competition every 12 years, treated equally to the other Firsts.
A Creo Aquam spell (Level 5) creating nonflammable grease from the caster's footsteps, leaving a slick area that forces Dexterity rolls.
Flaw a bacheler knight may take instead of Oath of Fealty.
Ancient inhabitants of the region who revered the boar and sacrificed to spirits and faeries.
A Virtue or Magic Quality named among the traits of magical animals or dragons in this text.
A Creo(Rego) Mentem 20 spell invented by Imanitos Mendax that implants information in a target who is then compelled to pass it on to friends.
A Major Virtue that a Bjornaer inner heartbeast may acquire (Ease Factor 30), also listed as a beast Virtue (e.g., immunity to fire or poison for a lizard).
A faerie-blooded folk witch councilor selling potions.
King of Norway killed at Stamford Bridge in 1066.
A cursed spirit at the center of a mobile regio (it, a host of the dead), tasked with guiding souls unable to reach Heaven onto their resting place.
Gruagachan nominally members of the Order of Hermes, taking the Hedge Wizard Flaw and Arcane Lore Virtue.
One of the two ethical viewpoints of House Tytalus's Philosophy of Conflict, represented by anticlockwise spiral symbolism indicating introspection.
Herd of magical horses (Might 10) of the Camargue led by the Great Stallion.
Kingdom known for the quality of its riding horses such as palfreys and jennets.
An Intellego Animal spell (Level 5) that gives a hazy mental image of an animal to which the caster has an Arcane Connection, useful for identifying an attacker.
A Minor General Flaw in which the character works poorly with others, treating his Leadership and Craft or Profession Abilities as three levels lower when collaborating.
A way to convert vis gained in the Magic Realm into knowledge of a single Magic Realm effect.
A woman living at the covenant of Semita Errabunda, named in an example command of a Psychomachia maleficium.
Followers of Joachim of Flora who have adopted strange beliefs about the Antichrist and the end of the age in 1260.
Free Mythic Companion Social Status Virtue required of all kabbalists.
Kingdom absorbed into the empire in 1033.
A hermit-wizard of the ancient Roman cult of Mithras who healed and trained the young Flambeau, later killed by sahirs in Iberia.
Archmaga and Quaesitor of House Guernicus, an Intellego specialist skilled in wards and necromancy, who calls the War Tribunal at Durenmar and co-leads the crusade.
A Minor Supernatural Virtue for corrupted beasts adding 2 to Infernal Might and granting an Infernal Power that cannot have a Penetration total.
Fourth rank (it), learns Inscription on the Soul and spends seven years at the temple.
(Organization) Lore of the Bologna learned-magician tradition, covering its charms, members, history and Initiation rites.
One of the capital vices, opposed by a holy temper.
A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character is intensely interested in supernatural and magical phenomena to the exclusion of other motivations.
The not completely evil, whose destination is Purgatory.
A Virtue the She-Wolf uses to train the magical wolves of the Majarida.
Religious who own no possessions personally or as a group, may beg, and answer to their own leaders and the pope rather than the local bishop.
A north Italian city near the iron mines of the southern Alps, famous for armaments and its capacity to produce enormous numbers of weapons to order.
Vassal of Oleron (1136-1182) built within a dam on the edge of the Morvan, destroyed when the dam burst.
Norse giants associated with Terram who have Terram Resistance.
Rare remaining magical and mysterious sites in Italy.
Templar chapterhouse in London on the Thames, seat of the English Master.
The Paris cathedral whose recently completed nave is 112 feet tall, with its chancellor wielding power over the university.
Templar commander of the delegation seeking magical aid for the Fifth Crusade.
The western group of the Western Islands, battered by Atlantic storms.
A major Social Status Virtue for a character with a large financial stake in a wealthy company, providing minor-noble-level income and the ability to act in any company role except capo.
Faerie leader of processions of the dead, collecting the dead and leading them to pagan underworlds.
Major Unholy Power Virtue granting the Supernatural Ability it at 1.
Wide channel separating Big Harcar from North Wamses.
A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character has a very hard time recalling one type of thing such as names, faces, or places.
Legendary realm of medieval fable used as a tonal model for an island-of-magicians saga.
Ability used to make verbal offers to Faerie.
A Creo Corpus spell (Level 20) granting a +9 bonus to Recovery rolls if maintained throughout the recovery interval.
ReMe 20 spell of Edwin's that rallies troops, granting Brave and Obedient traits.
A sports team consisting entirely of demons, captained by Hulikang.
Saint Power available through invoking Muslim holy forbears or relics.
Jewish atonement rite, a Divine-aligned version of Curse-Throwing, in which a goat is loaded with a community's sins on Yom Kippur and driven into desolation.
A town of Roman origin (Arae Flaviae) on the eastern edge of the Black Forest, overlooking the upper River Neckar, where butchers trained Rottweilers to pull carts.
Founder of the Gilbertines, died 1190 and canonized 1202; feast on February 4th.
A general Perdo Vim spell invented by Philippus Niger, like Demon's Eternal Oblivion but working on creatures with Magic Might.
Norse giants who can breathe underwater.
A Supernatural Ability granted by the Divine realm to feel the presence of good and evil in areas, persons, or objects, including detecting demons and angels.
Bond quality letting magus and familiar use each other's senses.
A supernatural event that destroyed the capacity of faeries to predict the future, perhaps an act of God.
Faeries dwelling in the regio of Oleron, some predating Hermetic colonization, who defend the covenant and can be awakened.
Ability appearing in character statistics in this text.
The Benedictine monk who came to convert the Saxons and founded the monastery and abbey at Canterbury that bears his name.
A saint whose Benedictine abbey lies in Chester; in legend she resurrected an eaten goose and forbade geese from entering a particular field forever.
A category of Flaw that draws characters into stories, such as family displeasure over Paid Rights or a female knight's unusual background.
Faerie bargaining art/Virtue for calling faeries and holding them in attendance to bargain; it Total is stress die + Presence + it + Faerie Rank + aura.
Roman author of the Germania, listed as a period source on the Germanic lands.
Encryption ledgers protecting Templar communications, kept secretly in provincial commanderies.

An infernal entity (Infernal Might 15, potential 60) manifesting as an ash seedling in the churchyard of Nortorf; prophesied to grow into a tree that will bring a king with fell powers if a black horseman defeats the white horseman.
The wild northeastern reaches of Germany between the Elbe and Oder, roamed by werewolves, witches, and giants, where pagan Slavic beliefs linger; claimed by the Rhine Tribunal.
A ReTe 5 Hermetic spell (R: Touch, D: Mom, T: Part) that magically opens any single lock regardless of complexity, named for Theodorus of Samos.
A Jerbiton league of merchant magi interested in gaining money through mundane trade and manipulating economies, seemingly based in the Rhineland.

text: A spell that animates a corpse into an automaton; such corpses use a revenant's physical statistics but are not supernatural and have no Might score or Magic Resistance.
The simultaneous attraction and repulsion between Faerie and the mundane world; entering Faerie requires it points equal to it strength.
A location in the Provencal Tribunal where the covenant of Tolosa Paratge resides.
Valuable buried objects collected by the coroner.
A Minor General Virtue: the character has found the one person meant for them, giving +3 to appropriate Personality Trait rolls; the it must be another player character with this Virtue.
A Major Story Flaw in which the character is a Christian who has never been baptized, often due to a supernatural background, and does not benefit from the sacraments.
A historical author (d. 1188) quoted from The Book of Learning by Example describing an angelic rescue on a mountain, illustrating the angel Nasir.
Gallic chieftain worshipped by the Bibracte cult.
Reward of glimpsing the Earthly Paradise after Purgatory.
A faerie merchant-scribe on Devil's Lane selling glamour books and exercise slates.
Minor Supernatural Flaw halving Lab Total for tattoos; gained via Shape initiation.
Grand Master (1210-1219) whose death led to Peter of Montaigu's election.
Identical faerie elves who create magic toys in the workshops.
